items.title: ‘Merry the Christmas Witch’ Director Estimated Movie Would Cost $80 Million — but Says With AI, He Made It for $1.5 Million (EXCLUSIVE)
items.excerpt: Director Tom Walsh said he produced the two-hour film for $1.5 million using AI, perhaps serving as a test case for the types of projects AI can help make.

items.title: Antonio Banderas to Star in AI-Powered Feature ‘Cortes’ From Utopai Studios
items.excerpt: The Oscar-nominated actor will star as Hernán Cortés in “Cortés,” an AI-powered feature from Utopai Studios and Ex Machina Studios now shooting in Paris.

items.title: Tilly Nollywood? African Filmmakers — Ready or Not — Get Set for the AI Revolution
items.excerpt: While generative AI has the potential to transform filmmaking in Africa, practical challenges on the continent abound.

items.title: AI Productions Require Traditional Skills To Be Cinematic, Say Filmmakers On Kling AI Panel: “You Need Experts To Prevent Everything Looking The Same”
items.excerpt: Filmmakers including '12.12: The Day' director Kim Sung-soo said on an ACFM & Kling AI panel in Busan that AI production still needs traditionally trained crew to keep results from looking the same.

items.title: Ben Affleck Used AI For "Lots Of Things" In Netflix's 'Animals'
items.excerpt: After selling his AI firm to Netflix earlier this year, Ben Affleck is showing off the tech in action on his latest directing project 'Animals'.

items.title: Netflix Has Used AI on About 300 Titles, but “Human Touch Is Critical,” Exec Says in Busan
items.excerpt: Netflix’s Asia-Pacific production head Sung Q Lee, ‘The Outlaws’ director Kang Yun-sung and Wētā FX's Kimball Thurston discussed creative possibilities, production savings and the limits of AI at the streamer’s Busan panel.

items.title: Busan’s Asian Contents & Film Market evolves with added focus on AI and microdramas
items.excerpt: Busan's ACFM (October 10-13) adds new programming on generative AI filmmaking and microdramas, including the InnoAsia tech strand and AI tool sessions.

items.title: My Screen Life: Taiwanese producer Patrick Mao Huang on spotting new talent and embracing AI
items.excerpt: Taiwanese producer Patrick Mao Huang talks spotting up-and-coming filmmakers and why he is embracing AI tools in production.

items.title: AI Creative Summit unveils full lineup for 2026 edition
items.excerpt: Presented by Screen International, Broadcast and Broadcast Tech, the AI Creative Summit is expanding this year in response to unprecedented interest in AI from the creative and media industries.

items.title: Aaron Sorkin Explains What AI Gets Wrong About Storytelling
items.excerpt: In a wide-ranging interview, Aaron Sorkin breaks down where AI-generated writing falls short of human storytelling craft.

items.title: Real-Time AI Worlds in Focus at Visko and Google Cloud's October 14 LA Fireside Chat
items.excerpt: The get-together looks at AI-generated environments that respond to user input while keeping continuity, and what they could mean for previs, virtual production and games.

items.title: Call for Participation: USC Annenberg AI in Film and TV Survey
items.excerpt: Dr. Stacy L. Smith's Inclusion Initiative is asking professionals above and below the line to share their thoughts on artificial intelligence in a 30-minute anonymous online questionnaire.

items.title: RevThink’s Revolve Accelerator Explores What Clients Value in the Age of AI
items.excerpt: RevThink’s six-week program for motion studio owners begins October 13, exploring how AI changes creative expertise and client value.

items.title: Retouch4me Lab: AI color correction for a whole shoot

items.title: You're Spending Too Much on Your AI Videos
items.excerpt: Curious Refuge shares workflows for saving generation credits on an AI film so you don't waste money on bad generations.

items.title: I Tested AI Agents Against a Real AI Artist
items.excerpt: Curious Refuge tests the top AI creative agents against a real AI artist's work and looks at new AI filmmaking tech.

items.title: Catherine Zeta-Jones Prefers "Real People" Over AI "Actors"
items.excerpt: Catherine Zeta-Jones wants to see fewer AI "actors" onscreen and more undiscovered human talent, weighing in on the synthetic-performer debate.
